sections.h2: One commercial painting contractor for many kinds of buildings
body: Commercial painting is a scheduling job first. A dental office cannot smell like paint at 8 a.m. A restaurant has to seat guests at 5 p.m. A warehouse cannot block its loading docks during a shipment window. As a commercial painting contractor in Gainesville, Ocala, and the surrounding counties, we build the work plan around those limits before we price the paint.
This page is the overview. Each type of facility has its own page with the details that matter for that building, so use the links below to go straight to the one that fits.

Stores, dining rooms, and kitchens: retail and restaurant painting

sections.h2: Inside or outside: two different kinds of commercial job
body: Interior commercial work is about staying out of the way of staff and customers: containing dust, protecting equipment, using low-odor coatings, and resetting rooms before the next business day. Our commercial interior painting page covers that in detail, including occupied medical and childcare spaces.

Exterior commercial work is about access, coatings, and traffic: lifts and scaffolding, tilt-wall and block surfaces, elastomeric and direct-to-metal coatings, and phased parking closures. See commercial exterior painting for how we handle storefronts and larger buildings. Many properties need both in the same year, and we can run them as one contract with one schedule, or split them so the exterior lands in the drier months and the interior follows.

We are licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, and every crew member is covered by workers' compensation. If your landlord, management company, or board needs it, we provide a certificate of insurance naming your entity before we mobilize. Our crews are our own; we do not subcontract the work.

The written proposal lists surfaces included and excluded, prep steps, primer and topcoat products by name, number of coats, and a working schedule. Nothing is added later without written approval. For buildings with several structures or tenants, we keep a record of colors and products so future touch-ups match the original.

We walk the property with your facility contact to map business hours, access points, alarm and key procedures, and spaces that need special care. From there we set a phased plan: nights, weekends, or zones painted in sequence so part of the building is always open. A single point of contact stays with the project from the walkthrough to the final punch walk, so your staff always knows who to call with a question about tomorrow night's work.

sections.h2: Planning repaints as part of building maintenance
body: For most businesses, paint is a maintenance item, not a one-time project. Lobbies, corridors, and break rooms wear fastest; exteriors on the sunny side of the building fade before the rest. Rather than repainting everything at once, many owners and managers set a rotating plan: high-traffic interior areas on a short cycle, full interiors less often, and exteriors when the coating starts to chalk or crack. An itemized proposal makes that easy, because each area is priced on its own line and can be moved to the next budget year.

Matching matters on a phased plan. When a hallway is repainted two years after the lobby, it should look like the same paint. We record the product, color formula, and sheen used in each area so later work lines up. The same record is useful if a tenant moves out and a single suite needs a quick turn.

We serve businesses and institutions across Alachua, Marion, Levy, Columbia, and Gilchrist counties. Local details are on our Gainesville commercial painting and Ocala commercial painting pages. Smaller towns get the same crews and the same written scope as the two big markets, whether the building is a clinic in Chiefland, a church in Trenton, or a storefront in Lake City. If an exterior also needs cleaning or graffiti protection, we can add pressure washing or an anti-graffiti coating to the same scope.

faqs.q: Can commercial painting be done at night or on weekends?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial work is scheduled around your operating hours, including nights and weekends, or phased by zone so the business stays open.

faqs.q: Will you provide a certificate of insurance before starting?
faqs.a: Yes. We are licensed, bonded, and fully insured with workers' compensation on every crew member, and we can issue a certificate naming your entity before mobilization.

faqs.q: What types of commercial buildings do you paint?
faqs.a: Offices, retail stores, restaurants, warehouses and industrial buildings, churches, schools, apartment communities, and HOA or managed properties, both inside and out.

faqs.q: Do you publish commercial painting prices?
faqs.a: No. Price depends on measured area, surface condition, product line, access and height, the number of colors, and scheduling needs like night work. The free written proposal itemizes each of these.
